definition: Calendar date to which the guest counts apply (documented as string YYYY/M/D). International: one row per nationality per date. Domestic: exactly one row per date.
audit_finding: Stored as real Excel datetimes, not strings. Daily, no gaps: train 2022-01-01→2025-07-31 (1,308 days), test 2025-08-01→2026-02-28 (212 days).

definition: TARGET VARIABLE. Total number of guests recorded for the nationality (international) or in total (domestic) on the given date.
dtype_units: integer, persons recorded on the date
missing_meaning: never missing in train; column ABSENT from both test files
audit_finding: Absent from both official test files (no observed target to score against). International minimum is exactly 10, and 238 nationality-day combinations (8 nationalities) have no row; suppression of small counts is a possible but unconfirmed explanation. Because New Arrivals (check-ins) are a subset that excludes continuing stays, Guests counts everyone recorded on the date; summed over days it approximates guest-nights (same-day visitors are included).

definition: Guests newly arrived (check-in) on the date, as opposed to continuing stays. Always a subset of Guests.
missing_meaning: empty cell = suppressed/unavailable (262 intl-train rows, 2 intl-test rows)
audit_finding: Verified ≤ Guests on every train row. Strong accounting link to Guests → allowed only in Competition mode, where the test files supply it. Test rows never have New Arrivals < 10, while 8.9% of intl-train rows do: the test extract was filtered differently (distribution shift).

definition: Guests who visited and departed on the same day without an overnight stay. International: '*' indicates zero, suppressed, or not applicable. Domestic: documented as always numeric.
missing_meaning: empty cell = '*' = zero OR suppressed OR n/a (cannot be distinguished)
audit_finding: Intl: 59.7% of train rows and 47.8% of test rows suppressed. Domestic: never missing (matches dictionary). Verified ≤ Guests and ≤ New Arrivals.

definition: Passport nationality / country of origin of the guests, uppercase ISO-style names. 45 distinct nationalities.
audit_finding: 45 nationalities, identical sets in train and test. 33 share a name with a flight 'Departure Country Name'; nationality is NOT the same concept as departure country.

definition: High-level residence group: 'International' (non-resident visitor) in the international files, 'Domestic' (resident / in-country) in the domestic files.
audit_finding: Constant within each file → carries no predictive information; used only to label scope.

definition: First day of the reporting month (e.g. '1/1/2022 12:00:00 AM' = January 2022) — documented as MONTHLY.
audit_finding: Granularity differs from the dictionary: 2022 = monthly (1 date per month, the 1st; 1,213 rows); 2023-01-01→2026-02-28 = DAILY (1,155 distinct days; 116,395 rows).

definition: Full name of the country from which the flight departs.
audit_finding: 33 countries; all 33 match a guest nationality by name. A departure country is where the flight originates, not the passengers' nationality (e.g. UK departures carry many non-UK nationals and 72% transfer traffic).

definition: City of origin; some countries have several departure cities.
audit_finding: Too granular to join to hotel data (no city in hotel files). Used via a derived 'active departure cities' count.

definition: Destination city; 'Abu Dhabi' in all observed records.
audit_finding: Verified constant = 'Abu Dhabi' on all 117,608 rows.

definition: Operating airline; 'Unknown' for a few unidentified records.
role: derived predictor (airline count, Etihad seat share)
audit_finding: Cannot be a direct feature at daily-aggregate grain (many airlines per day). Represented by active-airline count and Etihad Airways seat share.

definition: Average number of flights per week on the route during the reporting month. Dictionary: 'Populated with * in most observed rows … may not be available'.
audit_finding: Contradicts the dictionary: populated on 100% of daily rows. Value = flights_that_day × 7 / days_in_month exactly (max decode error 9e-16), giving an integer daily flight count (1–8). Frequency is therefore a validated feature for daily data.

definition: Point-to-point Business Class passengers (Abu Dhabi is their final destination). * = not available.
audit_finding: Populated on all daily rows. Cabin P2P counts sum to Total P2P on only 28.4% of rows (shortfall 1–28 pax, consistent with infants not being assigned a cabin). Totals are used instead.

definition: Business Class seats available on the route for the month. * = n/a (e.g. no Business cabin).
audit_finding: Daily rows: cabin capacities sum exactly to Total Seats on 100% of rows. 58.6% of daily rows have Business capacity > 0.

definition: Point-to-point Economy Class passengers for the route.
audit_finding: See Business Class P2P Count (cabin P2P ≠ Total P2P on 71.6% of rows).

definition: Economy Class seats available on the route.
audit_finding: Exact component of Total Seats on daily rows.

definition: Point-to-point First Class passengers; predominantly * (few routes offer First).
missing_meaning: empty on all 2022 monthly rows; zero where no First cabin
audit_finding: Daily rows are populated (zeros, not '*', where there is no First cabin).

definition: First Class seats available; predominantly * as most airlines do not operate First.
audit_finding: First capacity > 0 on only 5.4% of daily rows.

definition: Share of seat capacity occupied: Total PAX / Total Seats. Documented as a percentage string; values above 100% possible (overbooking / infant counting).
audit_finding: Stored as a numeric fraction, not a % string. Equals Total PAX / Total Seats to 1e-16 on every row. > 100% on 8.5% of daily rows (max 107.6%) and 1.1% of 2022 rows (max 185.7%). Aggregates are recomputed as ΣPAX / ΣSeats — never averaged.

definition: Point-to-point passengers across all cabins: journey originates at the departure city and terminates at Abu Dhabi.
audit_finding: The aviation quantity closest to potential hotel demand — but P2P includes residents returning home, VFR travellers and day visitors, so P2P ≠ hotel guests. 50.6% of daily PAX are P2P.

definition: All passengers on board across classes, including P2P and transfer/transit.
audit_finding: Identity verified on 100% of rows: Total PAX = Total P2P + Total Transfer + Total Transit.

definition: Total passengers minus lap infants; typically 1–5 below Total PAX.
audit_finding: Median 2 below Total PAX (max 31); never above it. Redundant with Total PAX.

definition: Total seat capacity offered across all cabins; the Load Factor denominator.
audit_finding: Exactly equals the sum of cabin capacities on daily rows. Mean 224 seats per decoded flight.

definition: Passengers who arrived on this route and transferred to another flight at Abu Dhabi (change of aircraft / flight number).
audit_finding: 49.4% of daily PAX. Transfer passengers connect onward and are not expected to stay in Abu Dhabi hotels (unless on a stopover — not identifiable in the data).

definition: Passengers in transit through Abu Dhabi (same aircraft / simpler connection). Mostly 0.
audit_finding: Zero on all but 3 of 116,395 daily rows (164 passengers, <0.001% of PAX) and non-zero on 4 monthly 2022 rows. No usable information → transit controls are disabled in the simulator.

definition: Business Class passengers who transferred at Abu Dhabi. * = not available.
audit_finding: Cabin transfer counts sum to Total Transfer on 58.6% of rows only.

definition: Economy Class passengers who transferred at Abu Dhabi. * = not available.
audit_finding: See Transfer Business Class Count.

definition: First Class passengers who transferred at Abu Dhabi. * = not available.
audit_finding: See Transfer Business Class Count.

definition: Business Class passengers in transit at Abu Dhabi. * = not available.
audit_finding: Cabin transit counts are > 0 on 3.6% of daily rows although Total Transit is zero on all but 3 rows — internally inconsistent; excluded.

definition: Economy Class passengers in transit at Abu Dhabi. * = not available.
audit_finding: See Transit Business Class Count.

definition: First Class passengers in transit (note the abbreviated name vs. the 'Class Count' pattern). * = not available.
audit_finding: Column name confirmed exactly as the dictionary warns ('Transit First Count').

definition: IATA code of the arrival airport; 'AUH' in all observed records.
audit_finding: Verified constant = 'AUH' on all rows.
